idea_name: Cross-pass end-PL normal PDF asymmetry as strategy-bias sensor
mechanism: Across N optimization passes collect each pass's final traded PL; fit a normal PDF (mean/Std) over that cloud. If the distribution mass and longer tail sit in the profit zone, treat the EA+parameter family as structurally right-skewed (mostly profitable passes); if mass/tail sit in the loss zone, treat it as a losing-biased search region. Overlay one-lot vs full-lot PDFs to separate lot-management effects from edge.
data_needed: Full optimization-pass PL endpoints (actual-lot and one-lot) persisted per pass; enough passes for a stable mean/Std estimate
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any EA under test; sample project 2MA_Martin; forward vs history passes stored separately
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a meta-sensor of whether a signal family's live parameter neighborhood is profit- or loss-asymmetric—usable as a robustness/regime-fitness flag when re-optimizing or retiring sleeves.
quote: If the larger tail and the distribution center are in the profit zone, the robot generates mostly profitable optimization passes and, accordingly, is good, otherwise it generates mostly unprofitable passes.

idea_name: Parametric absolute and growth VaR on deal PL series
mechanism: From the deal PL chart series compute mean Mx and Std; VaR(quantile)=f(quantile,Mx,Std) for q in {0.90,0.95,0.99}, reported both on absolute PL levels and on growth (returns). Persist VaR_absolute_* and VaR_growth_* per optimization pass alongside Sharpe/recovery/Altman Z.
data_needed: Ordered deal PL series (one-lot and managed-lot); risk-free rate r optional for related Sharpe charts
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any symbol in deal history; multi-symbol if EA traded spreads; history and forward segments
why_new_for_mis: Provides an in-terminal parametric VaR pair (level vs growth) as a rolling risk sensor of strategy P&L volatility that MIS can track as market conditions change.
quote: Parametric VaR is built using both absolute data and growth.

idea_name: Per-parameter win/loss frequency chart as sensitivity sensor
mechanism: After unloading optimization passes, group by a named input's discrete value; for each value build a distribution/frequency of profitable vs loss-making passes. Large shifts in win frequency across neighboring values mark high-sensitivity parameters; Filtre(from,till) then retains only passes inside stable ranges.
data_needed: OptimisationParams + ParamsCoefitients tables keyed by ID; parameter name/type registry; pass-level total_PL
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EA-agnostic; SQLite DB of optimization results; timeframe stored per pass (TF column)
why_new_for_mis: Turns optimizer grids into a parameter-sensitivity surface MIS can watch for brittle knobs—parameters whose win-rate collapses outside a narrow band flag fragile regime dependence.
quote: Another objective of this class is to create a graph displaying a frequency of profitable and loss-making trades for each individual optimization ratio value.

series_key: a new approach to custom criteria in optimizations
idea_name: NN activation soft-scores for optimizer criteria
mechanism: Article adapts ReLU/Softplus/Sigmoid/Tanh and their derivatives (shifted/corrected) to map TesterStatistics metrics into [0,1] soft scores for OnTester custom criteria, avoiding return(0) cliff effects in genetic search. No market-state sensor is constructed.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Optimizer statistics only (RF, trade count, etc.); no market instrument sensing
why_new_for_mis: No MIS sensing idea after full read—optimization scoring curves only.
quote: It occurs to me that if we can get a return value very close to 1 when the ratio or metric is at or above our desired minimum... we might be onto something...

series_key: building a candlestick trend constraint model
idea_name: Indicator-buffer gated entries under higher-TF trend constraint
mechanism: EA iCustom-loads Trend Constraint V1.09 and CopyBuffer on Buffer6 (sell) / Buffer7 (buy); those buffers already encode the series' D1 candlestick polarity constraint plus lower-TF confluence. One open position per MagicNumber; Boom 500 Index tester run. Part I wires the sensor; Part II restates the D1 gate explicitly.
data_needed: Trend Constraint indicator buffers 6/7; symbol ticks; SL/TP in points
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Boom 500 Index; PERIOD_CURRENT for EA; indicator uses D1 + lower TF internals from earlier parts
why_new_for_mis: Shows a clean buffer contract where a higher-TF candlestick regime is the hard gate for lower-TF signal emission—MIS can adopt D1 polarity as a first-class regime channel feeding any LTF sensor.
quote: An Expert based on the buffer6 and buffer7 of Trend Constraint V1.09

series_key: building a candlestick trend constraint model
idea_name: D1 open/close polarity as hard daily regime gate
mechanism: Each tick: is_bullish = daily_close > daily_open; is_bearish = daily_close < daily_open on PERIOD_D1 bar 0. Longs only when bullish AND RSI < oversold; shorts only when bearish AND RSI > overbought. Lower-TF RSI (PERIOD_CURRENT, default M1 in tester) supplies momentum confluence inside the D1 envelope.
data_needed: iOpen/iClose D1; iRSI on chart TF; RSI period and OB/OS thresholds
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Boom 500 Index; D1 for regime; M1 (tester) / PERIOD_CURRENT for RSI entries; 2023 backtest window shown
why_new_for_mis: A minimal, bar-native daily regime bit (candle color) that MIS can stream as a hard permission layer over any intraday sequence sensor without extra indicators.
quote: The day candlestick must be Bullish. On a lower time frame within a Bullish D1 candlestick, we need a confluence of signals. Specifically, the inbuilt indicator, such as the Relative Strength Index (RSI), should indicate an oversold condition

series_key: building a candlestick trend constraint model
idea_name: Close opposite positions on D1 polarity flip
mechanism: On each tick recompute D1 bullish/bearish; loop open positions and PositionClose any BUY when is_bearish or any SELL when is_bullish. Regime change itself is the exit trigger, independent of RSI. Trailing stop is separate profit lock.
data_needed: Live D1 open/close; open position tickets/types
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Boom 500 Index; D1 polarity; chart TF for management
why_new_for_mis: Treats daily candle color flip as an explicit regime-change exit sensor—MIS can broadcast D1 polarity transitions as force-flat events across sleeves.
quote: Close open positions if the trend changes... if ((position_type == POSITION_TYPE_BUY && is_bearish) || (position_type == POSITION_TYPE_SELL && is_bullish))

mechanism: In OnTick TrackSignalQualityMetrics once per bar: when the trend-filter slope changes direction, count bars elapsed since the most recent price pivot; accumulate Average Lag on Turns (Bars). Higher lag ⇒ slower confirmation of directional change across filter families (SMA/EMA/WMA/KAMA/DEMA/TEMA/ZLEMA/VIDYA/SAMA).
data_needed: Per-bar filter values and slope sign; detected price pivots; bar index clock
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1, AUDJPY H1 examples; multi-filter pullback EA; InSample/OutSample/Baseline phases
why_new_for_mis: Produces a continuous lag-to-confirm sensor of how late a smoother acknowledges turns—MIS can compare filters or watch lag inflate as a regime/responsiveness shift.
quote: Average Lag on Turns (Bars): When the filter slope changes direction, the framework measures how many bars have elapsed since the most recent price pivot. A higher value indicates the filter is slower to confirm directional change.

mechanism: Classify a filter slope change that reverses again within three bars as a whipsaw/false flip; increment False_Flips_Whipsaws. High counts quantify noise sensitivity of the filter line independent of P&L—usable as a choppiness/noise regime reading for that smoother.
data_needed: Filter slope sign series; 3-bar reversal window counter
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Same multi-filter demo (nine MAs including SAMA NLMS); H1 FX pairs in sample CSVs
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a filter-local noise sensor (whipsaw rate) that can flag choppy vs trending microstructure without relying on returns volatility alone.
quote: False Flips (Whipsaws): A slope change that reverses within three bars is classified as a whipsaw, incrementing a counter. This quantifies the filter's noise sensitivity.

idea_name: Price-to-filter intersection frequency and mean distance
mechanism: Per bar track (1) mean |close − filter| in points (Average Price-to-Line Distance) and (2) % of bars where close crosses the filter (Intersection Frequency). Very high intersect ⇒ over-reactive; very low ⇒ excessive lag; large distance ⇒ less price-tracking. Export alongside Sortino for cross-filter ranking.
data_needed: Close series and filter buffer each bar; point size
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD/AUDJPY H1 CSVs; SMA…SAMA filter set; ATR-based SL/TP multipliers in metrics struct
why_new_for_mis: Two cheap tracking-error sensors of how glued price is to a reference line—MIS can use intersect% and distance as adaptive-filter fitness under shifting regimes.
quote: Intersection Frequency (%): The percentage of bars on which the closing price crosses the filter line. A very high frequency suggests the filter is too reactive; a very low frequency may indicate excessive lag.

idea_name: Monoid-feature forecast of price-bar-range change for trailing
mechanism: Model decision columns as monoids (lookback∈{1..8}×4, TF∈{H1..D1}, applied price, indicator∈{RSI,Bollinger} regularized to 0–100 for decreasing→increasing range, decision∈{TREND,RANGE}). Operate monoids (LEAST/MOST/CLOSEST/FURTHEST) to pick settings that forecast bar-range change; feed forecast into CTrailingCT trailing stop. Tested EURUSD H1 with library RSI signal.
data_needed: OHLC for bar range; RSI and Bollinger outputs scaled 0–100; monoid identity/operation params
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD; H1 primary test 2022.05.01–2023.05.15; monoid TF set H1–D1 (actions extend to W1/MN1)
why_new_for_mis: Frames bar-range change as an explicit volatility sensing target driven by discrete monoid features—MIS can reuse the 0–100 range-direction score as a volatility-regime input to risk/trail logic.
quote: we want to forecast changes in price range, and use this in adjusting trailing stop of open positions.

idea_name: Correlation-weighted monoid-action expansion of sensitive features
mechanism: Correlate each monoid column's set values to observed price-bar-range changes; CorrelationInverted flag chooses whether to expand the most- or least-correlated column. Expand via monoid actions (larger lookback set, more TFs, PRICE_WEIGHTED, extra indicators) transforming the monoid without leaving the category-theory trailing class; re-test forecast accuracy.
data_needed: Per-column monoid values vs Δ(bar range); action-set arrays __LOOKBACKS_A / __TIMEFRAMES_A / __APPLIEDPRICES_A
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1; action TFs up to W1/MN1; prior-article feature stack
why_new_for_mis: A closed-loop way to grow the sensing feature set where sensitivity to volatility (bar-range) is highest—MIS can adopt correlation-to-target as a gate for expanding regime/vol feature vocabularies.
quote: we will be comparing the correlation of the monoid set values to changes in price bar range to get the weighting of each data-column.

idea_name: TREND vs RANGE monoid decision as regime feature
mechanism: Include a two-element monoid __DECISIONS = {TREND, RANGE} as a first-class feature alongside lookback/TF/price/indicator when forecasting bar-range changes. Feature-importance sketches (RF/permutation/etc.) treat this regime choice as a data-column whose weight informs whether range-expansion vs trend logic should dominate trailing adjustments.
data_needed: Discrete TREND/RANGE label per decision step; co-features and target Δ range
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Same EURUSD H1 trailing CT setup; indicator outputs regularized so 0=decreasing range, 100=increasing range
why_new_for_mis: Makes an explicit TREND/RANGE regime bit part of a volatility-forecast feature stack rather than only an entry filter—useful as a MIS regime channel coupled to range dynamics.
quote: And decision to range or trend.
